## Strategist — NO CHANGE
Caveat: could not read .agent-out files this run (path issue); worked from the decklist, thesis and two strategy queries. Argument, not evidence.
1. Pact of the Serpent: aimed at yourself naming Vampire it is the right refuel shape (strategy:card-advantage.plan-draw) but a sorcery that blanks right after a wipe (X = 0 or 1), the turn you most need cards. Aimed at an opponent: no — strategy:multiplayer.politics; handing a Goblin player X cards while you need the answer is a poor trade; a finisher only when the drain math already kills. Versus Champion of Dusk: Champion is a Vampire body (fuel, Skullclamp, drainers) and close on refuel; Pact is the weakest of the three on this board. Preacher stays: Seeker rewarding attacks does not make Preacher's connect easier, and Preacher is a Vampire body with repeatable draw.
2. Ruthless Lawbringer: Vampire, death trigger, third noncreature answer (strategy:deckbuilding.interaction-suite) — but sorcery speed, a sacrifice cost, fails on indestructible Purphoros; no redundant outlet to displace.
3. Viscera Seer not redundant (strategy:aristocrats: a free outlet fires in response to removal; the cheapest decoy). Twilight Prophet keep (ascend easy by T6-7). Bloodline Keeper keep (transform scales; tokens are fuel). Yahenni: no evidence it is worse. Deadly Dispute: no defensible cut.
4. Watch at the table: hellbent by T7-8 with Vampires on board (case for Pact/Champion later); an indestructible permanent blocking the game (case for Lawbringer or a non-destroy answer); whether Preacher draws on attack now that Seeker is in.
Open: research-strategy topic — how many free outlets a typal drain deck needs; Idol of Oblivion vs Champion for the refuel slot needs text + a scenario.

## Rules-question
Oracle (corpus): Pact of the Serpent — "Choose a creature type. Target player draws X cards and loses X life, where X is the number of creatures THEY control of the chosen type." Ruthless Lawbringer — "When this creature enters, you MAY sacrifice another creature. When you do, destroy target nonland permanent." Purphoros — indestructible; not a creature below devotion five.
(a) Pact at yourself: draw first, then lose life, in order (608.2c); X counts tokens and changelings (702.73a) as it resolves (ruling 2021-02-05); drawing past the library = loss at next SBA (104.3c / 704.5b).
(b) Pact at an opponent: they draw X AND lose X, draw first (608.2c); 0 or less life loses at the next SBA (704.5a). The draw happens even if the loss kills them.
(c) Lawbringer: reflexive trigger (603.12; ruling 2024-04-12), target chosen as it goes on the stack after the sacrifice, respondable. No other creature → nothing (608.2d). Tokens can be sacrificed (701.21a). Destroy fails on indestructible (702.12b). Purphoros as a non-creature enchantment is a legal "nonland permanent" target; the destroy still fails.
(d) A sacrificed token dies (700.4; 111.7 — triggers before it ceases to exist), so Blood Artist fires. Eminence triggers on CASTING Lawbringer (Vampire Assassin), not on entry — from Edgar's printed text; the CR DB has no eminence rule chunk.
Gap: Zulaport Cutthroat and Bastion of Remembrance not in the corpus for the agent's card-search; not cited.

contributions.text:
Asked: after five approved swaps, is there a sixth upgrade that FITS, or is the right answer no change. There is one, and it is modest and clean: Champion of Dusk in, Preacher of the Schism out. The axis is the one the thesis makes mandatory, draw, and the gap is shape rather than count. Enumerated from the branch's cards.json (sha 4783e555…, current): nine cards draw by oracle text — Black Market Connections, Caretaker's Talent, Crossway Troublemakers, Erebos, Liliana, Morbid Opportunist, Preacher of the Schism, Skullclamp, Welcoming Vampire — plus three that only select (Anje's and Bloodtithe Harvester's Blood tokens, Lethal Scheme's connive) and three tutors. Every one of the nine pays one card per event (Skullclamp two), eight of the nine need a board to fire, and NOT ONE scales with the board: the branch has zero 'draw X' refuel (Lethal Scheme's connive scales with its convokers, but connive is draw-then-discard — selection, net zero cards). That is the recon's first failure mode for this commander ('Vampire-count burst draw, which the branch has none of', as_of 2026-11-20) and the loss shape the log records four times (002 'vampires on board, nothing in hand', 003 'the finding, again', 006 'turn eight, nine, ten and not have enough cards in hand', 001 Champion of Dusk countered — 'the refuel that would have closed the game', the pilot 'would happily have paid the five life'). Champion over Pact of the Serpent, reversing my card-4/5 rank, for reasons specific to this list: Master of Dark Rites' BBB pays for Vampire, Cleric and Demon SPELLS only (deck-facts restricted_mana, verdict spells_only) — it casts Champion and never Pact; Urza's Incubator makes Champion {1}{B}{B}, Pact's own price, and does nothing for Pact; Champion is a Vampire spell, so with eminence live (Edgar in the command zone or on the battlefield) a token is down before it resolves and X is at least 2 on an empty board where Pact's X is 0 — the post-wipe case plan-draw warns about; and the Vampire count (28 in the 99) and the eminence trigger are unchanged Vampire-for-Vampire. Pact's aimed mode, priced as asked: the target loses X and DRAWS X; it is lethal only when X is at least their life (half of it with Bloodletter, since a sorcery always resolves on our turn), and a miss hands the one seat built to go wide X fresh cards. It is a kill condition with a punishing failure mode, and card 2 (Malakir Bloodwitch) already bought the Vampire-count each-opponent drain with no gift attached. On Preacher, the orchestrator's point is right and I say so: Sanctum Seeker made attacking correct, so Preacher's trigger fires more often than it did at card 4, and the 'combat-gated in a non-combat thesis' reason I gave then is weaker now. The cut stands on a different ground: per attack Preacher yields EITHER a 1/1 lifelink token (attacking the most-life opponent) OR one card for 1 life (while the pilot has the most life) — never both unless tied — which is the steady, board-dependent shape the branch has nine of and the corpus's rule for the last slots is to cut duplicated function first. It is contested, not easy. If the pilot wants every card to carry one of his four words, Champion carries none of them (it loses life, drains nobody) and NO CHANGE is the honest answer; stopping at five costs little. I recommend the swap because the one draw shape missing is the one the log keeps losing to. Removal is not re-opened: card 4 put the branch at seven true removal spells, and Ruthless Lawbringer (rank 4) closes a class the branch covers twice already. Deck-audit's figures below describe the SLEEVED v3.0.0 and are labelled so; no goldfish figure appears here, by the pilot's ruling.
